title: The debate of Seetha and Ravana is started,
introduction: The debate of Seetha and Ravana has started, as Ravana wished to woo Seetha. In the first instance Seetha believes him to be a Vedic Brahman but insists to know about him. Ravana reveals his identity and asks her to become his wife. Thereupon she goes into a frenzied state and brainstorms Ravana in all her curtness.
closing: These foots are said to be nonexistent in some more ancient mms. But lengthy narrations are there in calculating the age of Rama and Seetha, at this point of legend with these stanzas. The letter bhain the line mama bhartā mahātejāis the ninth letter of Gayatri hymn and thus the ninth book of Ramayana with thousand couplets is started from here. The whole of Ramayana is with twenty-four thousand verses and Gayatri hymn has twenty-four letters, and each book of Ramayana contains a thousand verses, starting with each letter of Gayatri. This is the then classification of the cantos of this epic and such grouping of verses is nonexistent now.
इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे सप्त चत्वारिन्शः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 47th chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
रावणेन तु वैदेही तदा पृष्टा जिहीर्षुणा |
परिव्राजक रूपेण शशंस आत्मानम् आत्मना
verses.iast:
rāvaṇena tu vaidehī tadā pṛṣṭā jihīr.hṣuṇā |
parivrājaka rūpeṇa śaśaṃsa ātmānam ātmanā
verses.translation: When Ravana whose intention is to abduct her has enquired thus, then on the basis of his Brahman friar's mien Seetha informed about herself on her own.

glosses.meaning: by one who wishes to steal
one who is asked, such Vaidehi

verses.devanagari:
ब्राह्मणः च अतिथिः च एष अनुक्तो हि शपेत माम् |
इति ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तम् तु सीता वचनम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
brāhmaṇaḥ ca atithiḥ ca eṣa anukto hi śapeta mām |
iti dhyātvā muhūrtam tu sītā vacanam abravīt
verses.translation: Thinking briefly that, 'he is a Brahman and an untimely guest, he will indeed curse me if he is not replied,' Seetha spoke this sentence.
notes: A lie cannot be uttered to a sanyaasi, much less to a Brahman. This friar appears as someone who is attired as a sanyaasi to fill his stomach. But he is Brahman, because he came booming Vedic hymns, which no other lesser Brahman can do. Thus, he is someone with a perfect Vedic background... and according to the saying: yatīnām pūjanam kāryam striyā vā puruṣena... ' an ascetic is to be revered either by a lady or a gentleman...' and thus he cannot be turned out saying 'my husband is not at home...' and if he is neglected he may curse...' these are the criss-cross thoughts of Seetha at that moment. Ghastly Viradha boldly carried her off at one time, but she is yet to see the cunningness of a demon. So with a half-belief and half-heart she started to talk to him.

verses.devanagari:
दुहिता जनकस्य अहम् मैथिलस्य महात्मनः |
सीता नाम्ना अस्मि भद्रम् ते रामस्य महिषी प्रिया
verses.iast:
duhitā janakasya aham maithilasya mahātmanaḥ |
sītā nāmnā asmi bhadram te rāmasya mahiṣī priyā
verses.translation: "I am the daughter of noble-souled Janaka, the king of Mithila, by name I am Seetha, and the dear wife and queen of Rama, let safety betide you.
notes: Here some versions use bhāryā'wife' while some use mahiṣī 'queen...' and this bhadram tecoupled with jihīrṣuṇā'abduction wisher...' is taken as a forewarning to Ravana, as she immediately says who her husband is, as she is aware that this friar is Ravana. Then it implicitly means 'you who wish to abduct me, think twice, for my husband is Rama, and let safety prevail on whole of your dynasty, for it is hard to deal with Rama or with his dear queen-wife...'

verses.devanagari:
उषित्वा द्वा दश समाः इक्ष्वाकूणाम् निवेशने |
भुंजाना मानुषान् भोगान् सर्व काम समृद्धिनी
verses.iast:
uṣitvā dvā daśa samāḥ ikśvākūṇām niveśane |
bhuṃjānā mānuṣān bhogān sarva kāma samṛddhinī
verses.translation: "On residing in the residence of Ikshvaku-s in Ayodhya for twelve years, I was in sumptuosity of all cherishes while relishing all humanly prosperities.
notes: Mythically Seetha is Goddess Lakshmi and an accorder of prosperity. Here she is saying that she had to enjoy 'humanly indulgences...' because her husband incarnated himself as a man, and since she had to enjoy along with him in her in-law's place, she enjoyed those luxuries. Or, if this is read as a+ mānuṣa bhogān'superhuman delights...' [of course, not 'inhuman delights...'] she enjoyed heavenly comforts as she was enjoying as Lakshmi in vaikunṭha 'Milky Ocean of Vishnu.' And then, she is indirectly telling Ravana that she has come now as Seetha, after immolating herself as Vedavati, in an earlier incarnation, only to end Ravana.

glosses.meaning: all, cherishes, in sumptuosity - I was.

verses.devanagari:
तत्र त्रयो दशे वर्षे राज अमंत्र्यत प्रभुः |
अभिषेचयितुम् रामम् समेतो राज मन्त्रिभिः
verses.iast:
tatra trayo daśe varṣe rāja amaṃtryata prabhuḥ |
abhiṣecayitum rāmam sameto rāja man.htribhiḥ
verses.translation: "In the thirteenth year the lordly king Dasharatha deliberated together with his imperial ministers to anoint Rama as Crown Prince of Ayodhya.

verses.devanagari:
तस्मिन् संभ्रियमाणे तु राघवस्य अभिषेचने |
कैकेयी नाम भर्तारम् मम आर्या याचते वरम्
verses.iast:
tasmin sambhriyamāṇe tu rāghavasya abhiṣecane |
kaikeyī nāma bhartāram mama āryā yācate varam
verses.translation: "When Raghava's anointment was being organised my venerable mother-in-law known as Kaikeyi begged her husband Dasharatha for a boon.

glosses.meaning: that, anointment, when being organised, but
of her husband - Dasharatha, boon, begged.

verses.devanagari:
प्रतिगृह्य तु कैकेयी श्वशुरम् सुकृतेन मे |
मम प्रव्राजनम् भर्तुर् भरतस्य अभिषेचनम्
द्वौ अयाचत भर्तारम् सत्यसंधम् नृपोत्तमम् |
verses.iast:
pratigṛhya tu kaikeyī śvaśuram sukṛtena me |
mama pravrājanam bhartur bharatasya abhiṣecanam
dvau ayācata bhartāram satyasaṃdham nṛpottamam |
verses.translation: "Restraining my veracious father-in-law by a good deed once done by her in his respect, Kaikeyi besought two boons from him, namely expatriation of my husband, and anointment of her son Bharata.

glosses.meaning: by good, deed [once done by Kaikeyi for Dasharatha]
truthfulness, abiding one, king, the best one, from such a husband - Dasharatha

verses.devanagari:
न अद्य भोक्ष्ये न च स्वप्स्ये न पास्ये कदाचन
एष मे जीवितस्य अन्तो रामो यदि अभिषिच्यते |
इति ब्रुवाणाम् कैकेयीम् श्वशुरो मे स पार्थिवः
अयाचत अर्थैः अन्वर्थैः न च यांचाम् चकार सा |
verses.iast:
na adya bhokṣye na ca svapsye na pāsye kadācana
eṣa me jīvitasya anto rāmo yadi abhiṣicyate |
iti bruvāṇām kaikeyīm śvaśuro me sa pārthivaḥ
ayācata arthaiḥ anvarthaiḥ na ca yāṃcām cakāra sā |
verses.translation: " 'If Rama is anointed now, come what may I will not eat, sleep, or drink, and my life ends this way,' thus Kaikeyi was adamantine, and the king and my father-in-law entreated her who is nagging with meaningful riches, but she did not make good on that entreaty.

glosses.meaning: in any way - come what may
of mine, he that, father-in-law, and king
she, that entreaty, not, made good.

verses.devanagari:
मम भर्ता महातेजा वयसा पंच विंशकः
अष्टा दश हि वर्षाणि मम जन्मनि गण्यते |
verses.iast:
mama bhartā mahātejā vayasā paṃca viṃśakaḥ
aṣṭā daśa hi var.hṣāṇi mama janmani gaṇyate |
verses.translation: "My great-resplendent husband was of twenty-five years of age at that time, and to me eighteen years are reckoned up from my birth.

glosses.meaning: by age, five, twenty - twenty-five years

verses.devanagari:
राम इति प्रथितो लोके सत्यवान् शीलवान् शुचिः
विशालाक्षो महाबाहुः सर्व भूत हिते रतः |
verses.iast:
rāma iti prathito loke satyavān śīlavān śuciḥ
viśālākṣo mahābāhuḥ sarva bhūta hite rataḥ |
verses.translation: "Rama - thus he is exalted in the world, an unambiguous, unblemished, unsullied one, and a broad-eyed ambidextrous one, who delights in bringing universal welfare, is my husband.
notes: The dexterity of an archer depends mainly on his sighting and targeting eye. Hence, the eyes and dexterity are to be coupled instead of cleaving them as two attributes of Rama. Otherwise, in Seetha's saying that 'my husband is a broad-eyed one...' it does not make any sense to Ravana, because Ravana's eyes are much more bigger and bloodshot. Thus 'my ambidextrous husband's eyes are broad puṇḍarīka viśāla akśaḥ,and those eyes are a couple of fish-eye lenses of a camera and can view in 360º, thus you cannot escape their target, in any angle...' Further, these and some more attributes in the coming verses like simha uraskaetc., they are the very same words coined by Sage Narada, while informing Valmiki about Rama in the first chapter of Bala Kanda. Some think such repetitions are essentially Homeric. But in Indian scripts they are not mere repetitions but reiteration of the very same concept in the very same words, which is not an epical flaw in view of the ruling ādarāt punarukti, ādarāt dvirukti...'an affectionate reiteration...' Hence, the very same words are put on the tongue of the principle character, Seetha.

glosses.meaning: all, beings, in welfare, delights in [delights in bringing universal welfare]

verses.devanagari:
कामार्तः च महाराजः पिता दशरथः स्वयम्
कैकेय्याः प्रिय कामार्थम् तम् रामम् न अभिषेचयत् |
verses.iast:
kāmārtaḥ ca mahārājaḥ pitā daśarathaḥ svayam
kaikeyyāḥ priya kāmārtham tam rāmam na abhiṣecayat |
verses.translation: "But Rama's father Dasharatha was lovesick for Kaikeyi and to fulfil her desired aspiration that great king did not anoint Rama.

glosses.meaning: one who is - love, sick - for Kaikeyi
for Kaikeyi's, cherish [aspiration,] desired [by her,] for fulfilling

verses.devanagari:
अभिषेकाय तु पितुः समीपम् रामम् आगतम्
कैकेयी मम भर्तारम् इति उवाच द्रुतम् वचः |
verses.iast:
abhiṣekāya tu pituḥ samīpam rāmam āgatam
kaikeyī mama bhartāram iti uvāca drutam vacaḥ |
verses.translation: "When Rama arrived in the presence of his father, Kaikeyi readily and decidedly spoke these words to my husband. [3-47-b, 14a]

verses.devanagari:
तव पित्रा समाज्ञप्तम् मम इदम् शृणु राघव
भरताय प्रदातव्यम् इदम् राज्यम् अकण्टकम् |
verses.iast:
tava pitrā samāGYaptam mama idam śṛṇu rāghava
bharatāya pradātavyam idam rājyam akaṇṭakam |
verses.translation: " 'What your father has proclaimed, oh, Raghava, that may be heard from me. He said, 'let this thornless kingdom be accorded to Bharata.'

verses.devanagari:
त्वया तु खलु वस्तव्यम् नव वर्षाणि पंच च
वने प्रव्रज काकुत्स्थ पितरम् मोचय अनृतात् |
verses.iast:
tvayā tu khalu vastavyam nava var.hṣāṇi paṃca ca
vane pravraja kākutstha pitaram mocaya anṛtāt |
verses.translation: "And you, oh, Kakutstha Rama, indeed have to inhabit the forests for nine plus five years, hence you repair to forests and redeem your father from the remorse of perjury.'

glosses.meaning: nine, five, also - nine plus five - fourteen
father, from untruthfulness, be released [redeemed from the remorse of perjury.]

verses.devanagari:
तथा इति उवाच ताम् रामः कैकेयीम् अकुतो भयः
चकार तत् वचः तस्या मम भर्ता दृढ व्रतः |
verses.iast:
tathā iti uvāca tām rāmaḥ kaikeyīm akuto bhayaḥ
cakāra tat vacaḥ tasyā mama bhartā dṛḍha vrataḥ |
verses.translation: " 'As an unfearing one from any quarter and as a resolute one in his pledge my husband Rama said 'so be it' to Kaikeyi and followed her dictate.

glosses.meaning: not, from anywhere, one who has fear - an unfearing one from any side, Rama
to her, to Kaikeyi, having said

verses.devanagari:
दद्यात् न प्रतिगृह्णीयात् सत्यम् ब्रूयात् न च अनृतम्
एतत् ब्राह्मण रामस्य व्रतम् ध्रुवम् अनुत्तमम् |
verses.iast:
dadyāt na pratigṛhṇīyāt satyam brūyāt na ca anṛtam
etat brāhmaṇa rāmasya vratam dhruvam anuttamam |
verses.translation: "My husband is evermore a renderer but not a recipient, and forever he speaks truth, and not the untruth, least of all. Oh, Brahman, this is the unalterable and unsurpassable vow of Rama.
notes: In Maha Bharata Dharmaraja is informed that 'a king shall give, but he shall not beseech, he can perform a Vedic Ritual but cannot make it performed by others, he can learn Veda-s, but cannot teach them, he shall endeavour to govern the people [properly...] dadyāt rājā na yāceta yajeta na yājayeta | na adhyāpayet adhiyīta prajān ca paripālayet || bhārata - rāja dharma

glosses.meaning: not, in turn, takes [not a recipient]
un, truth, not, also [least of all]

verses.devanagari:
तस्य भ्राता तु वैमात्रो लक्ष्मणो नाम वीर्यवान्
रामस्य पुरुषव्याघ्रः सहायः समरे अरिहा |
verses.iast:
tasya bhrātā tu vaimātro lakṣmaṇo nāma vīryavān
rāmasya puruṣavyāghraḥ sahāyaḥ samare arihā |
verses.translation: "One known as Lakshmana is such a Rama's brother from another mother, and he is a valorous one, tigerly-man, and an eliminator of enemies in war.
notes: A stepmother is called as vi mātaor dvaimātaand it is said vaimātreyo vimātṛja - amara kośaone is other mother, the other is second-mother, both are the nomenclatures of a stepmother.

verses.devanagari:
स भ्राता लक्ष्मणो नाम धर्म चारी दृढ व्रतः
अन्वगच्छत् धनुष् पाणिः प्रव्रजंतम् मया सह |
verses.iast:
sa bhrātā lakṣmaṇo nāma dharma cārī dṛḍha vrataḥ
anvagacchat dhanuṣ pāṇiḥ pravrajaṃtam mayā saha |
verses.translation: "He who is known as Lakshmana, a follower of virtue and steadfast in his commitment, followed Rama handling his bow as a helpmate, when Rama was proceeding to forests along with me.
notes: Some texts use the word brahma cārī'celibate' basing on the word Rama used when saying about Lakshmana to Shuurpanakha about Lakshmana as apūrvīwhile some others use as above.

verses.devanagari:
जटी तापस रूपेण मया सह सह अनुजः
प्रविष्टो दँडकारण्यम् धर्म नित्यो धृढ व्रतः |
verses.iast:
jaṭī tāpasa rūpeṇa mayā saha saha anujaḥ
praviṣṭo da.ṇḍakāraṇyam dharma nityo dhṛḍha vrataḥ |
verses.translation: "Because Rama always abides in probity and resolutely vowed to it, he entered Dandaka forest in the aspect of a tufty haired saint along with me and his brother.

glosses.meaning: in probity, always [one who is abiding]

verses.devanagari:
ते वयम् प्रच्युता राज्यात् कैकेय्याः तु कृते त्रयः
विचराम द्विज श्रेष्ठ वनम् गंभीरम् ओजसा |
verses.iast:
te vayam pracyutā rājyāt kaikeyyāḥ tu kṛte trayaḥ
vicarāma dvija śreṣṭha vanam gambhīram ojasā |
verses.translation: "Such as we are, oh, eminent Brahman, we three are moving about the impenetrable Dandaka forest just by our own mettle as we fell down from kingdom owing to Kaikeyi.

glosses.meaning: those, we- such a we are we
for Kaikeyi, sake of, but for
impenetrable, forest, we are moving about.

verses.devanagari:
समाश्वस मुहूर्तम् तु शक्यम् वस्तुम् इह त्वया
आगमिष्यति मे भर्ता वन्यम् आदाय पुष्कलम् |
रुरून् गोधान् वराहान् च हत्वा आदाय अमिषान् बहु
verses.iast:
samāśvasa muhūrtam tu śakyam vastum iha tvayā
āgamiṣyati me bhartā vanyam ādāya puṣkalam |
rurūn godhān varāhān ca hatvā ādāya amiṣān bahu
verses.translation: "Be comfortable for a moment, here it is possible for you to make a sojourn, and soon my husband will be coming on taking plentiful forest produce, and on killing stags, mongooses, wild boars he fetches meat, aplenty.

glosses.meaning: by you, here, to take rest, possible
mongooses like [civet-like mammals of the family Viverridae, esp. of the genus Herpestes, Marathi manguus]

verses.devanagari:
सः त्वम् नाम च गोत्रम् च कुलम् आचक्ष्व तत्त्वतः |
एकः च दण्डकारण्ये किम् अर्थम् चरसि द्विज
verses.iast:
saḥ tvam nāma ca gotram ca kulam ācakṣva tattvataḥ |
ekaḥ ca daṇḍakāraṇye kim artham carasi dvija
verses.translation: "Such as you are, oh, Brahman, you may make mention of your name, parentage and caste, in their actuality. For what reason you are wandering in Dandaka forest lonesomely?" Thus Seetha questioned Ravana.
notes: She is addressing him as 'oh, Brahman...' and yet asking his caste. This is a tricky stanza. This implies her knowledge and/or ignorance about Ravana. As a housewife, it is a natural question to be put to an out-of-way friar moving in the deep of forests. Here, neither a village, nor a single family, nor even a human being is available to accord alms, and this odd almsman is moving here who is supposed to move about villages as said:bhikśa artham grāmam praviśet.. Or, she must be asking him about his caste, creed etc., when he was a householder. But it is out of place. On the other hand, if Seetha is from a well-trained family, she is not supposed to question the caste, creed, and name of a real sanyaasi. Again, she is asking him to reveal himself 'in essence, truthfully.' She might have thought him to be a cursing Brahman in the first instance, but she might have found him out to be a pseudo-sanyaasi. Now that she is slowly realising that he may not be a proper Brahman either, she may be asking him straightforwardly. Because Ravana is coming out of Brahman's guise in next two stanzas, it is said that she pointedly asked him as above.

glosses.itrans: naama ca gotram ca kulam ca
glosses.iast: nāma ca gotram ca kulam ca
glosses.devanagari: नाम च गोत्रं च कुलं च
glosses.meaning: name, also, parentage, also, caste, also

verses.devanagari:
एवम् ब्रुवत्याम् सीतायाम् राम पत्नीआम् महाबलः |
प्रत्युवाच उत्तरम् तीव्रम् रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
verses.iast:
evam bruvatyām sītāyām rāma patnīām mahābalaḥ |
pratyuvāca uttaram tīvram rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
verses.translation: Ravana, the great-mighty king of demons, brusquely replied Seetha, the wife of Rama, while she is still speaking in this way.

verses.devanagari:
येन वित्रासिता लोकाः स देव असुर मानुषा |
अहम् सः रावणो नाम सीते रक्षो गण ईश्वरः
verses.iast:
yena vitrāsitā lokāḥ sa deva asura mānuṣā |
aham saḥ rāvaṇo nāma sīte rakṣo gaṇa īśvaraḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, Seetha, of whom all the worlds composed of gods, demons and humans are highly startled, I am that sovereign of hosts of demons, known as Ravana.

glosses.meaning: he that, demon, hosts, sovereign of

verses.devanagari:
त्वाम् तु कांचन वर्ण आभाम् दृष्ट्वा कौशेय वासिनीम् |
रतिम् स्वकेषु दारेषु न अधिगच्छामि अनिन्दिते
verses.iast:
tvām tu kāṃcana varṇa ābhām dṛṣṭvā kauśeya vāsinīm |
ratim svakeṣu dāreṣu na adhigacchāmi anindite
verses.translation: "On seeing you, oh, impeccable one, glittering with golden complexion and attired in ochry-silks, I derive no pleasure in my wives.
notes: Ravana as a devotee of Lakshmi said the above as a renouncer. tvām dṛṣṭvā'on seeing you...' after a long time... svakeṣu'in my kith and kin...' dāreṣuwives...' ratim'pleasure, involvement...' na adhigacchāmi'not, I attain...' 'On seeing you, I no longer can attain pleasure with my kith and kin, or with my wives... for I have seen my ultimate motherly goddess... thus I am ready to renounce this accursed being of Ravana...' Maheshvara Tirtha.

verses.devanagari:
बह्वीनाम् उत्तम स्त्रीणाम् आहृतानाम् इतः ततः |
सर्वासाम् एव भद्रम् ते मम अग्र महिषी भव
verses.iast:
bahvīnām uttama strīṇām āhṛtānām itaḥ tataḥ |
sarvāsām eva bhadram te mama agra mahiṣī bhava
verses.translation: "You become my prime queen above all the choicest women with superior status, whom I have appropriated from here and there.
notes: Ravana as devotee is saying: āṛtānām uttamam strīṇām 'To all of the choicest women appropriated by me...; mama to me'; agra mahiṣīyā 'to the one who is my prime queen'; tasyāḥ ca mama ca to her and to me; bhava īśvarī you be the ruling deity; 'To all of the choicest women appropriated by me... and to the one who is my present prime queen, namely Mandodari, to her and to me, and to all of us, you be the ruling deity...' Tiirtha.

verses.devanagari:
लंका नाम समुद्रस्य मध्ये मम महापुरी |
सागरेण परिक्षिप्ता निविष्टा गिरि मूर्धनि
verses.iast:
laṃkā nāma samudrasya madhye mama mahāpurī |
sāgareṇa parikṣiptā niviṣṭā giri mūr.hdhani
verses.translation: "Nestled on a mountaintop my great city known as Lanka is there in the midst of an ocean and all over encompassed by an ocean.

verses.devanagari:
तत्र सीते मया सार्धम् वनेषु विचरिष्यसि |
न च अस्य वन वासस्य स्पृहयिष्यसि भामिनि
verses.iast:
tatra sīte mayā sārdham vaneṣu vicariṣyasi |
na ca asya vana vāsasya spṛhayiṣyasi bhāmini
verses.translation: "Oh, Seetha, there you can saunter in pleasure-gardens along with me, and oh, lady with resentment, you will not think back to this forest-living, at all events.
notes: The word bhāmini is an addressing to a beautiful lady, who is with some anger or resentment kopanā sā eva bhāminī - amara kośa and Ravana mistook Seetha's fury as 'an anger in passion.'

glosses.meaning: not, also - at all events, think back to.

verses.devanagari:
पंच दास्यः सहस्राणि सर्व आभरण भूषिताः |
सीते परिचरिष्यन्ति भार्या भवसि मे यदि
verses.iast:
paṃca dāsyaḥ sahasrāṇi sarva ābharaṇa bhūṣitāḥ |
sīte paricariṣyanti bhāryā bhavasi me yadi
verses.translation: "Oh, Seetha, if you become my wife five thousand handmaidens adorned with ornaments of every description will be in your attendance." Thus Ravana said to Seetha.
notes: Ravana, the devotee, is saying panca sahasrāṇi dāsyaḥ 'five thousand servants...' me 'with me... together with me' paricariṣyasi yadi tava 'if we all render service to you...' then you will be bāryā; bha + āryā; bhāyā= kāntyā, āryā= pūjyā 'by your splendour...' bhavasi you will become the venerable Goddess Lakshmi by your own splendour while thousands are serving you...'

verses.devanagari:
रावणेन एवम् उक्ता तु कुपिता जनक आत्मजा |
प्रत्युवाच अनवद्यांगी तम् अनादृत्य राक्षसम्
verses.iast:
rāvaṇena evam uktā tu kupitā janaka ātmajā |
pratyuvāca anavadyāṃgī tam anādṛtya rākṣasam
verses.translation: When Ravana said in this way, Seetha the daughter of Janaka, a flawless one by her physique, dishonoured and replied that demon.
notes: Here the word tu in rāvaṇena evam uktā tu is said as tu śabdena pūrvokta upacāra vacana vilakśaṇa vacana it means ultimately as - Seetha spoke in derision.

glosses.meaning: by Ravana, this way, she who is said, but
without, not, appreciable, limbed - one with flawless limbs - Seetha

verses.devanagari:
महा गिरिम् इव अकंप्यम् महेन्द्र सदृशम् पतिम् |
महा उदधिम् इव अक्षोभ्यम् अहम् रामम् अनुव्रता
verses.iast:
mahā girim iva akampyam mahendra sadṛśam patim |
mahā udadhim iva akṣobhyam aham rāmam anuvratā
verses.translation: "I have avowed to adhere to such a husband Rama, who is inflexible like a sturdy mountain, comparable to lordly Indra, unshakable like a vast ocean.
notes: Vividly: 'A mountain will be unswerving even if a hundred thunderbolts strike it at once, thus is my husband... but you, you are always swerving while hankering after your petty cherishes... thus, you are a straw in the wind... my husband is a coequal of Indra, while you are humiliated by Indra's son. The ocean will be turbulent on its surface but it will be calm and clear at its abyss, engulfing unusual treasures... though my husband appears as a passionate person, an indulgent person in humanly pursuits, from hunting games to hollering, in worldly agonies and ecstasies, but at his heart, he is like the fathomless serene ocean... I have avowed to follow him in this lifetime.'

glosses.meaning: not, be roiled - be churned - unshakeable
I, follow up on [adhere,] avowed to.

verses.devanagari:
सर्व लक्षण संपन्नम् न्यग्रोध परि मण्डलम् |
सत्य संधम् महाभागम् रामम् अनुव्रता
verses.iast:
sarva lakśaṇa sampannam nyagrodha pari maṇḍalam |
satya saṃdham mahābhāgam rāmam anuvratā
verses.translation: "He who is enriched with all endowments, and who is like a banyan tree with its surmounted orbicularity, the high-minded one with truthfulness alone is his target, and I am avowed to adhere to such a Rama.
notes: The banyan tree is an Indian fig tree, Ficus benghalensis, the branches of which hang down and root themselves. The simile of a banyan tree to Rama says that: he is an atom in the atomic seed of that tree. On its growth, it spreads so wide and broad and every branch take its own root like the manifold growth of this universe. Hence, every individual being is his offspring and progeny. And the whole universe is pervaded by his 'tree-top' like shelter. Secondly, that tree gives shelter to innumerable beings for it is so wide at its apex. Hence, anyone can take shelter under Rama, because he is obliged to oblige all sarva jana anukūlata as said in an ancient saying: kūpa udakam vaṭa ccāyā yuvatīnām stana dvayam | śītā kāle bhavet uṣṇam uṣṇa kāle bhavet śītalam || 'water in a well, banyan tree shade, maiden's two breasts, will warm up in cold season and cool down in hot season...' Govindaraja.

glosses.meaning: to such a Rama., I avowed to adhere.

verses.devanagari:
महाबाहुम् महोरस्कम् सिंह विक्रांत गामिनम् |
नृसिंहम् सिंह संकाशम् अहम् रामम् अनुव्रता
verses.iast:
mahābāhum mahoraskam siṃha vikrāṃta gāminam |
nṛsiṃham siṃha saṅkāśam aham rāmam anuvratā
verses.translation: "He who is ambidextrous, broad-chested, supreme among men, and a lion-like person with the strides of prancing lion, and I am avowed to adhere to such a Rama.
notes: 'His dexterity is evident from the moment he started to save the order of universe, at the time churning Milky Ocean, becoming Mohini, becoming a Fish, a Tortoise etc. His strides are evident, when he as a dwarfish boy strode all the three worlds. As a lion-man, he tore the very stomach of the evil and now he is striding like a prancing lion towards you, for you alone are the prey for that lionised human incarnation...'

glosses.meaning: man, lion [here, not exactly a lion, the best, foremost, supreme one]
to such a Rama, avowed to adhere.

verses.devanagari:
पूर्ण चन्द्र आननम् वीरम् राज वत्सम् जितेन्द्रियम् |
पृथु कीर्तिम् महाबाहुम् अहम् रामम् अनुव्रता
verses.iast:
pūrṇa candra ānanam vīram rāja vatsam jitendriyam |
pṛthu kīrtim mahābāhum aham rāmam anuvratā
verses.translation: "He who is a valiant one with a face like that of full-moon, a prince with his self-conquered, and he who is expressly acclaimed and effectively armed, and I am avowed to adhere to such a Rama.
notes: 'He is a valiant person and he confronts, if need be, his enemies straightforwardly, about which you have heard when your Khara, Dushana, and others are eliminated by him... but you are sneaky and slithery... you are ever a thief, never a valiant one... his face is like a pleasant full-moon, at any given opportunity, while yours is revulsive... and you are like the eclipsing planet Rahu or Ketu, whose effect lasts a few minutes... he is expressly acclaimed for his welfare activities and of course, you are also expressly acclaimed, but, only for your ill-faring actives... the senses of an yet to be crowned prince will be like the unbridled horses... but my husband conquered his own senses like an uncrowned sagacious emperor... while you, though you declare yourself as the monarch of demons, there is not even an iota of self-righteousness in you, befitting even to a petty king... then where is the question of your majesty, monarchy, or sovereignty...'
Seetha reiterates the statement 'I am avowed to adhere to such a Rama...' four times. This is dārḍhyata- said for the purpose of 'reinforcement' of her statement.

glosses.meaning: to such a Rama, avowed to adhere.

verses.devanagari:
त्वम् पुनः जंबुकः सिंहीम् माम् इह इच्छसि दुर्लभाम् |
न अहम् शक्या त्वया स्प्रष्टुम् आदित्यस्य प्रभा यथा
verses.iast:
tvam punaḥ jambukaḥ siṃhīm mām iha icchasi durlabhām |
na aham śakyā tvayā spraṣṭum ādityasya prabhā yathā
verses.translation: "You being a fox you woo me who am an absolutely inaccessible lioness? Why wooing, it is impossible for you to touch me as with the untouchable Shine of the Sun.
notes: A fox usually waits in a ditch until the lion or lioness finishes its feast. The lion will have its lion's share and go away. Then the lioness and her cubs have their share and go away. Then it is the day of the fox-in-the-ditch. 'Like a fox-in-the-ditch, how you dare to come to an inaccessible lioness, when the lion departed...' Next, Sun's wife is Prabha or Shine and she is non-figural resplendent entity. She is perceivable but untouchable. If anyone can lay his hands on her by the dint of his yogic or ascetic practises, and if he baskets that Shine for use in night, that night becomes a day, for it will be shining with sunshine, and thus his pleasurable night is evanished. Thereby he looses his minimal personal comfort of a night and it will be self-ruinous to experiment with such ideas.

glosses.meaning: you [being a fox,] again [on the other hand, yet]
I, by you, to touch - to seize

verses.devanagari:
पादपान् कांचनान् नूनम् बहून् पश्यसि मंदभाक् |
राघवस्य प्रियाम् भार्याम् यः त्वम् इच्छसि राक्षस
verses.iast:
pādapān kāṃcanān nūnam bahūn paśyasi maṃdabhāk |
rāghavasya priyām bhāryām yaḥ tvam icchasi rākśasa
verses.translation: "You who are an ill-fated demon, oh, demon, by your wooing the dear wife of Raghava, thus you must be visualising many golden trees, undeniably.
notes: A dying person fantasises golden trees and the like presuming his travel to heaven. By these illusions his death is predictable.

glosses.meaning: which, you are - you who are

verses.devanagari:
क्षुधितस्य च सिंहस्य मृग शत्रोः तरस्विनः |
आशी विषस्य वदनात् दम्ष्ट्राम् आदातुम् इच्छसि
verses.iast:
kṣudhitasya ca siṃhasya mṛga śatroḥ tarasvinaḥ |
āśī viṣasya vadanāt damṣṭrām ādātum icchasi
verses.translation: "Do you wish to twitch fangs from the mouth of a ravenous lion, the expeditious challenger of animals, and from the mouth of a rebounding venomous serpent.
notes: The simile of lion and serpent is to Rama and the fangs to Seetha. A lion or a snake knows well how to protect its instruments, namely fangs. Hence, Seetha is the fang of expeditious and ravenous Rama in eliminating evil on earth and now he will become a grudging venomous cobra too, for its tail is going to be trampled, by Seetha's abduction. Thus, the instrumentality of Seetha is established and no instrument needs to bother on its own, because its owner takes care of that instrument.

glosses.meaning: expeditious ones [expeditious lion and rebounding serpent]
fangs, to twitch, do you wish to?

verses.devanagari:
मंदरम् पर्वत श्रेष्ठम् पाणिना हर्तुम् इच्छसि |
काल कूटम् विषम् पीत्वा स्वस्तिमान् गंतुम् इच्छसि
verses.iast:
maṃdaram parvata śreṣṭham pāṇinā hartum icchasi |
kāla kūṭam viṣam pītvā svastimān gaṃtum icchasi
verses.translation: "Do you wish to steal away the massive Mandara Mountain by the sleight of your hand, but how do you wish to decamp healthily without consuming lethal poison?
notes: She is reminiscing her emergence. Mt. Mandara is mentioned but not Mt. Himalayas or Mt. Meru, even though they are more massive and lofty. Vishnu used Mt. Mandara as a churn-staff when Milk Ocean was churned, but not Himalayas or Meru and the burden of that Mt. Mandara was sustained by Vishnu alone as a Tortoise, which is impossible for simpletons like Ravana, as Ravana failed to lift Mt. Kailash. Before Lakshmi's emergence from the churning Milk Ocean, Her elder sister haalaahala 'lethal poison' emerged and it could be contained only by Shiva, and now, if Ravana contemplates to consume her elder sister kaalakuuTa, haalaahala 'lethal poison' it is evident what will become of him. This is nidarśana alankāra; samānya vākyārtha aikyata 'aesthetics of correspondence...'

glosses.meaning: by [the sleight of] hand, to steal, do you wish to
healthily, to go [decamp,] you wish to?

verses.devanagari:
अक्षि सूच्या प्रमृजसि जिह्वया लेढि च क्षुरम् |
राघवस्य प्रियाम् भार्याम् अधिगंतुम् त्वम् इच्छसि
verses.iast:
akṣi sūcyā pramṛjasi jihvayā leḍhi ca kṣuram |
rāghavasya priyām bhāryām adhigaṃtum tvam icchasi
verses.translation: "If you wish to override the dear wife of Raghava, then it is as good as wishing to deeply scrape your eyes with needlepoint, and licking the razorblade with your tongue.

glosses.meaning: to over, ride - steal off, [if,] wish to
eyes, verily [deeply,] you wish to wipe [scrape]

verses.devanagari:
अवसज्य शिलाम् कण्ठे समुद्रम् तर्तुम् इच्छसि |
सूर्या चन्द्रमसौ च उभौ प्राणिभ्याम् हर्तुम् इच्छसि
यो रामस्य प्रियाम् भार्याम् प्रधर्षयितुम् इच्छसि |
verses.iast:
avasajya śilām kaṇṭhe samudram tartum icchasi |
sūryā candramasau ca ubhau prāṇibhyām hartum icchasi
yo rāmasya priyām bhāryām pradhar.hṣayitum icchasi |
verses.translation: "You who wish to bitterly intimidate the dear wife of Rama are as good as the one who wish to swim an ocean arraying a boulder around his neck, and with a pair of hands you wish to steal away both the Sun and Moon?

glosses.meaning: at neck, boulder, arraying - like dress material
ocean, to swim for it, you wish to
with a pair of you hands, to steal, you wish to.

verses.devanagari:
अग्निम् प्रज्वलितम् दृष्ट्वा वस्त्रेण आहर्तुम् इच्छसि
कल्याण वृत्ताम् यो भार्याम् रामस्य हर्तुम् इच्छसि |
verses.iast:
agnim prajvalitam dṛṣṭvā vastreṇa āhartum icchasi
kalyāṇa vṛttām yo bhāryām rāmasya hartum icchasi |
verses.translation: "You who wish to abduct me with an auspicious legend as the wife of Rama, thus you wish to steal away a glowing fire in a cloth-bundle, though evincing it to be highly flaming?

glosses.meaning: wife, to abduct, you wish to
by cloth [bundle,] to steal away, you wish to.

verses.devanagari:
अयो मुखानाम् शूलानाम् अग्रे चरितुम् इच्छसि |
रामस्य सदृशीम् भार्याम् यो अधिगंतुम् त्वम् इच्छसि
verses.iast:
ayo mukhānām śūlānām agre caritum icchasi |
rāmasya sadṛśīm bhāryām yo adhigaṃtum tvam icchasi
verses.translation: "You who wish to override the befitting and selfsame wife of Rama, are wishing to tread on the needle-sharp spikes of iron spears. [3-47-44b, c]
notes: This declaration that she is selfsame to Rama is on the analogy of rāmā the feminal name of Rama. aham nārāyanī nāma sā sattā vaiṣṇavī parā - lakṣmī tantra 3-1 - yahā mayā jagat vyāptam svarūpeṇa svabhāvataḥ | tayā vāptam idam viśvam niyantrī ca tathā īśvarī || 'I am indeed Naaraayanee [i.e. Lakshmi] the supreme essence of Lord Vishnu----Lakshmi Tantra 3.1. 'In my essence and entity I pervade all this universe, and as I pervade all over I am the controller and presiding deity...'

glosses.meaning: iron, faces, spears, top of [on spiculated floor, sharp spikes of iron spears]

verses.devanagari:
यद् अंतरम् सिंह शृगालयोः वने
यद् अंतरम् स्यन्दनिका समुद्रयोः |
सुर अग्र्य सौवीरकयोः यद् अंतरम्
तद् अंतरम् दाशरथेः तव एव च
verses.iast:
yad aṃtaram siṃha śṛgālayoḥ vane
yad aṃtaram syandanikā samudrayoḥ |
sura agrya sauvīrakayoḥ yad aṃtaram
tad aṃtaram dāśaratheḥ tava eva ca
verses.translation: "Which odds are there between a lion and a fox in a given forest, which odds are there between a turbid-rivulet and an ocean, and which odds are there between a fine-wine and sour-gruel, likewise you are also at odds with the son of Dasharatha.
notes: The usage of the word syandanika is said to be the usage of a rare word by Valmiki, meaning kśudra nadi 'a turbid-rivulet...' as recorded by Pt. Satya Vrat, in Ramayana - A Linguistic Study.

glosses.meaning: between turbid-rivulet, ocean, which, odds - are there

verses.devanagari:
यद् अंतरम् कांचन सीस लोहयोः
यद् अंतरम् चन्दन वारि पंकयोः |
यद् अंतरम् हस्ति बिडालयोः वने
तद् अंतरम् दशरथेः तव एव च
verses.iast:
yad aṃtaram kāṃcana sīsa lohayoḥ
yad aṃtaram candana vāri paṃkayoḥ |
yad aṃtaram hasti biḍālayoḥ vane
tad aṃtaram daśaratheḥ tava eva ca
verses.translation: "Which imparity is there among the metals of gold and lead, which imparity is there among the waters of sandalwood and sewage, which imparity is there between an elephant and a wildcat of forests, such an imparity exists between you and the son of Dasharatha.

glosses.meaning: which, imparity = which, imparity is there
among you, Dasharatha's son, like that, also.

verses.devanagari:
यद् अंतरम् वायस वैनतेययोः
यद् अंतरम् मद्गु मयूरयोः अपि |
यद् अंतरम् हंस गृध्रयोः वने
तद् अंतरम् दाशरथेः तव एव च
verses.iast:
yad aṃtaram vāyasa vainateyayoḥ
yad aṃtaram madgu mayūrayoḥ api |
yad aṃtaram haṃsa gṛdhrayoḥ vane
tad aṃtaram dāśaratheḥ tava eva ca
verses.translation: "Which dissimilarity obtains betwixt a crow and an eagle, which dissimilarity obtains betwixt a waterfowl and a peacock, which dissimilarity obtains betwixt a swan and a falcon living in forest, such a dissimilarity obtains betwixt you and the son of Dasharatha.

glosses.meaning: betwixt Dasharatha's son, yours, like that, only

verses.devanagari:
तस्मिन् सहस्राक्ष सम प्रभावे
रामे स्थिते कार्मुक बाण पाणौ |
हृता अपि ते अहम् न जराम् गमिष्ये
वज्रम् यथा मक्षिकया अवगीर्णम्
verses.iast:
tasmin sahasrākṣa sama prabhāve
rāme sthite kārmuka bāṇa pāṇau |
hṛtā api te aham na jarām gamiṣye
vajram yathā makṣikayā avagīrṇam
verses.translation: "Even if you steal me away now, later when Indra similar Rama posits himself with his bow and arrows in hand on the battlefield, you cannot live on, and in the meanwhile you cannot digest me, as with a diamond swallowed along with a fly." Thus Seetha gave her vent to her disdainful feelings towards Ravana.
notes: Here, if a fly is accidentally swallowed along with pure ghee, it will be vomited out for the nausea caused by that fly in the stomach. But diamond rends the stomach. The word vajram is usually a diamond, and if a diamond is consumed, accidentally or wilfully, it will tear off the intestines to death. Hence taking the Vedic saying vajro va ājyam the word is generally translated as ghee.

glosses.meaning: Thousand-eyed one, Indra similar, with impaction

verses.devanagari:
इति इव तत् वाक्यम् अदुष्ट भावा
सुदुष्टम् उक्त्वा रजनी चरम् तम् |
गात्र प्रकंपात् व्यथिता बभूव
वात उद्धता सा कदली इव तन्वी
verses.iast:
iti iva tat vākyam aduṣṭa bhāvā
suduṣṭam uktvā rajanī caram tam |
gātra prakampāt vyathitā babhūva
vāta uddhatā sā kadalī iva tanvī
verses.translation: On speaking these sentences with high-strung words, with all her unsullied intentions to that highly sullied night-rambler Ravana, her fragile body trembled tormentedly as with a banana plant up-heaved by gust.
notes: She poured forth all of her feelings unbothered for consequences and when her haranguing is over, she felt certain uneasiness. This uneasiness is two fold. One is in accordance with humanly nature of a woman as she is staunch enough to not yield to any, and if anyone makes an untoward advance, she has a 'list' of suicide-programs, those that are narrated to Lakshmana in the previous chapter. Further, she is yet to know about Rama's welfare, which will be impossible if this demon carries her away now. On the other side, as a Divine Consort of Vishnu, her uneasiness is for her separation from Rama, but not from the fear of any molestation by Ravana, and as the expected hour has come, the expectancy for the prospective elimination of Ravana is making her to tremble, impetuously.

ताम् वेपमानाम् उपलक्ष्य सीताम्
स रावणो मृत्यु सम प्रभावः |
कुलम् बलम् नाम च कर्म च आत्मनः
समाचचक्षे भय कारण अर्थम्
verses.iast:
tām vepamānām upalakṣya sītām
sa rāvaṇo mṛtyu sama prabhāvaḥ |
kulam balam nāma ca karma ca ātmanaḥ
samācacakṣe bhaya kāraṇa artham
verses.translation: On closely marking Seetha to be tremulous, he that Ravana whose impetus is Death similar, clearly informed her of his name, caste, competency, and capability as his purpose is to cause scare.
